page: Amazon Web Services r9g.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server type powered by the AWS Nitro System and custom 64-bit Arm-based AWS Graviton processors. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs matching 16 physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz, running a single hardware thread per core. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a generous 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio (8.0 GB per core) designed for applications with heavy working memory footprints.

Storage and network architectures rely entirely on external and fabric connections. The r9g.4xlarge configuration features no local instance storage, requiring persistent data to reside on networked block volumes. The Nitro-managed network interface offers a baseline throughput of 8 Gbps. The instance contains zero discrete GPUs, focusing entirely on memory density and core-isolated compute efficiency.

Due to its non-hyperthreaded physical core architecture and large memory capacity, the r9g.4xlarge minimizes resource contention across concurrently running processes. This profile makes it well suited for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory datastores, distributed caching layers, relational database engines, extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines, and memory-bound enterprise data analytics.
description: Amazon Web Services r9g.4xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit Arm AWS Graviton processors. Configured with 16 dedicated physical cores at 3.3 GHz and 16 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, the server supplies 128.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It contains no onboard local storage, depending on network-attached block volumes, and includes no discrete GPU hardware. Network operations are supported by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth profile. The combination of dedicated core execution and high memory capacity ensures consistent processing for memory-bound applications without noisy-neighbor thread interference. The r9g.4xlarge is primarily suited for large in-memory databases, distributed caches, real-time analytics engines, and transactional database services requiring substantial memory overhead.
